blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A master's plan puts the outage jobs of projects A, B, C and D in 2029, and the CP-SAT check says they cannot all be scheduled that year. No smaller conflict is searched for. Which row does the loop add?

options.says: The no-good on a failed set S has right-hand side |S| - 1; with all four jobs in S that is 3, not 2.
That refuses plans with only some of the four in 2029, which may schedule; the cut must allow them.
Right: the no-good is the sum over the failed set S at most |S| - 1, here 4 - 1 = 3; it forbids exactly the failed combination in that year.
That pushes jobs into the failed year; the no-good is a <= row on the failed set.

origin.section: A Subproblem Solved by Any Method Can Still Return a Cut

questions.stem: An LBBD master already holds a 52-week row per year, yet the loop still needs many iterations, and every conflict it finds is two long jobs whose windows lie in the same short season. Which row added to the master should save the most iterations?

options.text: Per year, the weeks of the year's jobs at most 52, entered a second time
options.says: A copy of a row that does not bind changes nothing; the page's 52-week row saved no iterations.

options.text: Per year and season, the weeks of jobs touching the season at most its length
options.says: A job whose window reaches outside the season can run outside it; counting it refuses plans that schedule.

options.text: Per year and season, the weeks of jobs inside the season at most 52 weeks
options.says: A season is far shorter than 52 weeks, so this row refuses nothing the 52-week row did not.

options.text: Per year and season, the weeks of jobs inside the season at most its length
options.says: Right: it states the real clash, as the season rows did, and refuses only plans that cannot be scheduled.

origin.section: A Relaxation of the Subproblem in the Master Saves Iterations

questions.stem: On a small instance an LBBD loop ends at 22,817, while one CP-SAT model of the whole problem reports OPTIMAL at 22,950, and its plan passes a plain-Python check of every rule and every year's schedule. What does this point to?

options.text: A cut or relaxation row in the loop refused a plan that can be scheduled
options.says: Right: the loop's master refused a feasible plan worth more, so one of its rows is not valid.

options.text: The loop is right: a decomposition's optimum is the more exact of the two
options.says: A feasible plan worth 22,950 exists, so an optimum of 22,817 is wrong; on the lesson's instance both methods agree.

options.text: The one model is wrong: it leaves out the season window of each job
options.says: Each job's start variable in the one model runs from its release to its deadline minus its length, so seasons are kept; and its plan passed an independent check of every rule.

options.text: Both are right: two optimal plans of one instance can differ in value
options.says: Two optimal plans may differ, but by definition their values are equal.

origin.section: One CP-SAT Model of the Whole Problem Checks the Answer
